title: The Bike That Makes AliExpress Look Pointless...

takeaways.text: Carbon frame, fork, seatpost and integrated carbon bar with Shimano 105 2×12 for just under £1,400 in the UK, cheaper than a Canyon Endurace CF 5 or Ribble all-road Tiagra.

His size-XL (roughly 56 cm) loan bike weighed 8.9 kg; much of the weight is in deep alloy wheels with 24 steel spokes, narrow 21 mm rims and 28 mm Maxxis Detonator tires, which feel sluggish accelerating.
Maximum clearance is 32 mm, fine for road but less than he expects of an all-road bike.
No creaks, a stiff integrated cockpit and snappy bottom-bracket area with a compliant rear from dropped seatstays and seatpost flex; the 105 groupset needed no adjustment out of the box.

Teardown: press-fit BB86 shell not fully faced but square, sound-deadening foam on internal lines, faced brake mounts, clean internals with a few bladder wrinkles, and a heavy (just over 900 g) SENICX crankset as the only non-105 drivetrain part.
An internal ridge in the seat tube stops the seatpost from going lower, so riders needing a low saddle may have to cut the post; the bar tape may be wrapped in the wrong direction.

disclosure: The bike was lent by V-Ride, SUNPEED's UK distributor, and the video offers a 5% discount code through it.
summary: A ride review and teardown of the SUNPEED Invincible Sport carbon road bike with Shimano 105 R7120 and alloy wheels, as sold in the UK.
